item.title: Camel & Horse Riding on the Tottori Dunes — Guide
item.description: One of the most popular things to do at the Tottori Sand Dunes is to ride a camel across the sand — a nod to the dunes' desert-like character and one of the few places in Japan you can do it. Operators near the main dune entrance offer short guided rides on Bactrian (two-humped) camels, led on foot by a handler, as well as photo sessions where you sit on a camel against the backdrop of the dunes and sea.

item.title: Cycling Naoshima Art Island — Guide
item.description: Naoshima is small enough to explore by bicycle, and renting one is one of the best ways to experience the art island. With a bike — standard or electric-assist, useful for the island’s hills — you can move freely between the Benesse Art Site museums, the Art House Project in the old village, Kusama’s yellow and red pumpkins, quiet beaches and coastal viewpoints, all at your own pace and without waiting for buses.

item.title: River Kayaking and Canyoning in Saga — Guide
item.description: For an active, adventurous side of Saga, the rivers and gorges of the mountainous south offer kayaking and canyoning. Guided kayak tours let you paddle across calm rivers and reservoirs among forested hills, gliding on clear water and taking in the peaceful scenery at your own pace — suitable for beginners with a guide. For more of a thrill, canyoning (or ‘shower climbing’) tours take you into the mountain gorges to scramble, wade, slide down natural rock chutes and jump into clear pools beneath waterfalls, wearing a wetsuit and helmet — a wet, exhilarating way to experience the wild river landscape.

item.title: Sandboarding on the Tottori Dunes — Guide
item.description: Sandboarding — snowboarding’s desert cousin — is one of the most fun and accessible activities at the Tottori Sand Dunes. You strap onto a board and slide down the steep slip-face of a dune, with the soft sand making for gentle, forgiving landings that suit total beginners and children. Local operators run guided lessons that include the board, basic instruction and the walk back up, on a slope steep enough to be genuinely exciting.

item.title: Sea Kayaking Around Naruto — Guide
item.description: The coast around Naruto, where the Seto Inland Sea meets the Pacific, offers scenic sea kayaking amid island scenery, quiet coves and views of the great Onaruto Bridge. Guided kayak tours let you paddle the calmer sheltered waters away from the fierce tidal race of the strait itself, gliding along the coastline, exploring inlets and small beaches, and taking in the sea and bridge from water level. Suitable for beginners with a guide, it’s a peaceful yet active way to experience the beautiful Naruto seascape up close, quite different from the roar of the whirlpools nearby.

item.title: Sea Kayaking in the Seto Inland Sea — Guide
item.description: The Seto Inland Sea off Imabari, with its calm sheltered waters, gentle tides and countless small islands, is one of the loveliest places in Japan for sea kayaking. Guided kayak tours let you paddle out among the islands of the Shimanami Kaido area, gliding across clear blue water, exploring hidden coves and pebble beaches, and passing beneath the soaring spans of the great suspension bridges from water level — a completely different perspective on the famous cycling route.
